1: Welcome to the story deck for Building Global Secure Access, a developer workbook in the Federal Modernization Workbook.
Instead of nine chapters one at a time, we'll follow one pilot ring all the way through: a fictional agency tenant, contoso dot example, on November 16, 2026, and the same tenant two weeks later.
Every value comes from the kit's own test fixtures, and every output on a slide is what the kit really printed.
One note before we begin: the workbook is a draft awaiting review, and the code is illustrative, tested against fixtures, not against a lyve tenant.

Ring 1 goes lyve, in a test tenant first and then production, with one settings file per environment and the same commands.
Before any change, a read-only preflight checks the stage, the collection, the emergency group's exclusion from every network policy, the logs, and the approved decisions.

The runbook hasn't been run against a lyve tenant.

That's the pilot ring, end to end: decided honestly about what G C C does and doesn't state, logged before anything was enforced, measured device by device, changed only through plans a second person approved, enforced only when report-only was clean, and recorded as evidence an assessor can check.
